messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, so each operation rounds the exact real‑valued sum to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can introduce a small error, the error incurred by adding a and b first may differ from the error incurred by adding b and c first. Consequently \((a+b)+c\) and \(a+(b+c)\) can produce different rounded results, breaking associativity.
